code_first.q: Use decomposition and abstraction to identify the essential inputs in an image-size calculation.
code_first.code:
width = 12
height = 10
depth = 4
bits = width * height * depth
print(bits)
p: Predict the number of raw image bits.
Explain which three inputs are essential and why the file name is irrelevant.
code_first.a: 12 × 10 × 4 = 480 bits. At 8 bits/pixel, the output is 960 bits. Width, height and colour depth are essential; the filename does not change the raw pixel-data calculation. The result excludes headers/compression.
